en bugt.explanation: "En bugt" means "a bay". It has a second meaning, "a bend", as in a river. To say there is a bend in a river, use the same word: "en bugt i floden" (a bend in the river).

en bule.explanation: "En bule" means "a dent". It also means "a bump" on the body. To say you have a bump on your forehead, use the same word: "en bule i panden" (a bump on the forehead).

en bums.explanation: "En bums" means "a pimple". To say where a pimple is, add the place: "en bums i panden" (a pimple on the forehead).

en bund.explanation: "En bund" means "a bottom", as in the lowest part of something. To say something lies at the lowest point of the sea, say: "på bunden af havet" (on the bottom of the sea). The word is also in "en tærtebund" (a pie base).

en bundlinje.explanation: "En bundlinje" means "a bottom line". It is built from "bund" (bottom) and "en linje" (a line).

en bunke.explanation: "En bunke" means "a pile". To talk about a pile of clothes, say: "en bunke tøj" (a pile of clothes). To say someone has a large amount of money, use the same word: "en bunke penge" (a large amount of money).

en burger.explanation: "En burger" means "a burger". To name a burger without meat, put the main ingredient first: "en vegetarburger" (a vegetarian burger).

en bus.explanation: "En bus" means "a bus". To say you travel by bus, use "at tage" (to take): "Jeg tager bussen" (I take the bus).

en busbillet.explanation: "En busbillet" means "a bus ticket". It is built from "bus" (bus) and "en billet" (a ticket); "billet" is also in "en biografbillet" (a cinema ticket) and "en koncertbillet" (a concert ticket).

en buschauffør.explanation: "En buschauffør" means "a bus driver". It is built from "bus" (bus) and "en chauffør" (a driver); "chauffør" is also in "en taxachauffør" (a taxi driver) and "en lastbilchauffør" (a truck driver).

en busk.explanation: "En busk" means "a bush". To name a bush by the flower it carries, put the flower first: "en rosenbusk" (a rose bush).

en butik.explanation: "En butik" means "a shop". To name a shop by what it sells, put the goods first: "en blomsterbutik" (a flower shop).

en butiksansat.explanation: "En butiksansat" means "a store employee". It is built from "en butik" (a shop) and "ansat" (employed).

en butiksindehaver.explanation: "En butiksindehaver" means "a shop owner". It is built from "en butik" (a shop) and "en indehaver" (a holder). To say who holds a card, "indehaver" works on its own: "indehaveren af kortet" (the holder of the card).

en butikskæde.explanation: "En butikskæde" means "a store chain". It is built from "en butik" (a shop) and "en kæde" (a chain); "kæde" is also in "en hotelkæde" (a hotel chain) and "en cykelkæde" (a bicycle chain).

en butterfly.explanation: "En butterfly" means "a bow tie". To talk about the insect, use "en sommerfugl" (a butterfly): "En sommerfugl sidder på blomsten" (A butterfly is sitting on the flower).

en by.explanation: "En by" means "a town". The same word also means "a city". To call a big place a city, say: "København er en by" (Copenhagen is a city). To say you are in town, use "i byen": "Jeg er i byen" (I am in town).

en bydel.explanation: "En bydel" means "a district". It is built from "en by" (a town) and "en del" (a part); "del" is also in "en landsdel" (a region of a country) and "en verdensdel" (a continent).

en byfest.explanation: "En byfest" means "a town festival". It is built from "en by" (a town) and "en fest" (a party); "fest" is also in "en fødselsdagsfest" (a birthday party).

en byge.explanation: "En byge" means "a shower", as in a short spell of rain. For the shower you wash in, use "et brusebad": "Jeg tager et brusebad" (I take a shower).

en byggeplads.explanation: "En byggeplads" means "a construction site". It is built from "bygge" (build) and "en plads" (a place); "plads" is also in "en parkeringsplads" (a parking lot) and "en legeplads" (a playground).

en bygherre.explanation: "En bygherre" means "a developer", as in the person or company that orders a building. It is built from "bygge" (build) and "en herre" (a lord).

en byrde.explanation: "En byrde" means "a burden". To say someone is carrying a burden, use "at bære på" (to carry): "Han bærer på en stor byrde" (He is carrying a big burden).

en bytteseddel.explanation: "En bytteseddel" means "a gift receipt". It is built from "at bytte" (to swap) and "en seddel" (a slip); "seddel" is also in "en pengeseddel" (a banknote).

en båd.explanation: "En båd" means "a boat". To talk about a large ship, use "et skib" (a ship): "Skibet sejler til Norge" (The ship sails to Norway).

en bæk.explanation: "En bæk" means "a brook". To talk about a bigger stream, use "en å" (a small river): "Åen løber gennem byen" (The river runs through the town).

en bæltetaske.explanation: "En bæltetaske" means "a fanny pack". It is built from "et bælte" (a belt) and "en taske" (a bag); "taske" is also in "en skoletaske" (a school bag) and "en indkøbstaske" (a shopping bag).

en bænk.explanation: "En bænk" means "a bench". To name a bench by its place, put the place first: "en parkbænk" (a park bench).

en bærbar computer.explanation: "En bærbar computer" means "a laptop". "Bærbar" is built from "at bære" (to carry) and "-bar" (-able). To say "the laptop", add an "e" to "bærbar": "den bærbare computer".

en bæver.explanation: "En bæver" means "a beaver". To name the dam a beaver builds, say: "en bæverdæmning" (a beaver dam).

en bøde.explanation: "En bøde" means "a fine", as in a penalty for breaking a rule. To say you have to pay one, use "at betale" (to pay): "Jeg skal betale en bøde" (I have to pay a fine). The word is also in "en parkeringsbøde" (a parking fine).

en bøf.explanation: "En bøf" means "a steak". For a patty of ground meat, use "en hakkebøf" (a ground beef patty): "Jeg spiser en hakkebøf med løg" (I am eating a ground beef patty with onions).

en bøg.explanation: "En bøg" means "a beech". The beech is the national tree of Denmark.

en bøjle.explanation: "En bøjle" means "a hanger". The same word is in "en tandbøjle" (braces for teeth).

en bøjning.explanation: "En bøjning" means "an inflection", as in grammar. To show how a verb changes, take "at spise" (to eat): "spiser", "spiste" and "spist" (eats, ate, eaten) are its inflections. To talk about a physical bend, use "en knæbøjning" (a knee bend), which comes from "at bøje" (to bend).

en bølge.explanation: "En bølge" means "a wave", as in the sea. The word is also in "en hedebølge" (a heat wave) and "en kuldebølge" (a cold wave).

en bølgelængde.explanation: "En bølgelængde" means "a wavelength". It is built from "en bølge" (a wave) and "en længde" (a length).

en bøn.explanation: "En bøn" means "a prayer". It also means "a plea". To say you ask for help with strong feeling, use "en bøn om hjælp" (a plea for help). The plural "bønner" is also the plural of "en bønne" (a bean): "Jeg spiser bønner" (I am eating beans).

en børnehave.explanation: "En børnehave" means "a kindergarten". In Denmark it is for children from about three to six, before school starts. It is built from "børn" (children) and "en have" (a garden).

en børnelæge.explanation: "En børnelæge" means "a pediatrician". It is built from "børn" (children) and "en læge" (a doctor); "læge" is also in "en dyrlæge" (a vet).

en børnemenu.explanation: "En børnemenu" means "a kids' menu". It is built from "børn" (children) and "en menu" (a menu); "menu" is also in "en frokostmenu" (a lunch menu).

en børste.explanation: "En børste" means "a brush". The same word is the base of the verb "at børste" (to brush): "Jeg børster tænder" (I brush my teeth).

et bad.explanation: "Et bad" means "a bath / shower". To say you swim in the sea or a lake, use the verb "at bade" (to bathe): "Vi bader i havet" (We are swimming in the sea).

et badekar.explanation: "Et badekar" means "a bathtub". It is built from "bad" (bath) and "et kar" (a tub).

et badested.explanation: "Et badested" means "a swimming spot". It also means "a seaside resort". To say a place is a seaside resort, use the same word: "Blokhus er et badested" (Blokhus is a seaside resort). It is built from "bad" (bath) and "et sted" (a place).

et badeværelse.explanation: "Et badeværelse" means "a bathroom". It is built from "bad" (bath) and "et værelse" (a room). To ask where a public toilet is, use "toilettet" (the toilet): "Hvor er toilettet?" (Where is the toilet?).

et bagagebånd.explanation: "Et bagagebånd" means "a baggage carousel". It is built from "bagage" (baggage) and "et bånd" (a belt); "bånd" is also in "et målebånd" (a measuring tape) and "et løbebånd" (a treadmill).

et bagagerum.explanation: "Et bagagerum" means "a trunk", as in the back of a car. It is built from "bagage" (luggage) and "et rum" (a room), so literally it is a "luggage room".

et bageri.explanation: "Et bageri" means "a bakery". It comes from the verb "at bage" (to bake). At a bakery in Denmark you can buy "wienerbrød" (literally, Vienna bread), which English speakers call a Danish pastry.

et baghold.explanation: "Et baghold" means "an ambush". To say someone waits hidden to attack, use "at ligge i baghold" (to lie in ambush): "Soldaterne lå i baghold" (The soldiers lay in ambush).

et bal.explanation: "Et bal" means "a ball", as in a formal dance. For the round ball you kick, use "en bold" (a ball): "Han sparker til bolden" (He kicks the ball).

et band.explanation: "Et band" means "a band". For a ribbon or tape, use "et bånd" (a ribbon): "Hun binder et bånd i håret" (She ties a ribbon in her hair). The plural is "bands", with an s as in English.

et barn.explanation: "Et barn" means "a child". To talk about more than one, use the irregular plural "børn" (children): "Vi har to børn" (We have two children).

et barnebarn.explanation: "Et barnebarn" means "a grandchild". It is built from "et barn" (a child) twice, so literally it is a "child's child". To talk about more than one, use the irregular plural "børnebørn" (grandchildren): "Jeg har fire børnebørn" (I have four grandchildren).

et batteri.explanation: "Et batteri" means "a battery". To say a battery is dead, use "fladt" (literally, flat): "Batteriet er fladt" (The battery is dead).

et bed.explanation: "Et bed" means "a flower bed". For a bed to sleep in, use "en seng" (a bed): "Jeg sover i min seng" (I sleep in my bed).

et bedrag.explanation: "Et bedrag" means "a deception". For the crime of cheating someone out of money, use "et bedrageri" (a fraud): "Politiet efterforsker et bedrageri" (The police are investigating a fraud). The word is also in "selvbedrag" (self-deception).

et bedrageri.explanation: "Et bedrageri" means "a fraud". It comes from the verb "at bedrage" (to deceive).

et begreb.explanation: "Et begreb" means "a concept". To say you have no idea about something, use "ikke have begreb om" (to have no idea about): "Jeg har ikke begreb om, hvad det koster" (I have no idea what it costs).

et behov.explanation: "Et behov" means "a need". To say you need something, use "at have behov for" (to have a need for): "Jeg har behov for hvile" (I need rest).

et belæg.explanation: "Et belæg" means "a basis / evidence". To ask someone to back up a claim, say: "Har du belæg for det?" (Do you have grounds for that?).

et beløb.explanation: "Et beløb" means "an amount of money". For an amount of other things, use "en mængde" (a quantity): "en stor mængde vand" (a large quantity of water).

et ben.explanation: "Et ben" means "a leg / bone". Danes say "benet" (the leg) where English says "his leg": "Han har brækket benet" (He has broken his leg). To talk about the bone of the upper leg, use "et lårben" (a thigh bone).

et besøg.explanation: "Et besøg" means "a visit". To say you are visiting someone, use "på besøg": "Jeg er på besøg hos min mor" (I am visiting my mother).

et betalingskort.explanation: "Et betalingskort" means "a payment card". It is built from "en betaling" (a payment) and "et kort" (a card). A well-known Danish payment card is the "Dankort".

et bevis.explanation: "Et bevis" means "a proof". It also means "evidence". To say the police have no evidence, say: "Politiet har ingen beviser" (The police have no evidence).

et bibliotek.explanation: "Et bibliotek" means "a library". To say you are at the library, use "på biblioteket": "Jeg er på biblioteket" (I am at the library).

et bibliotekskort.explanation: "Et bibliotekskort" means "a library card". It is built from "et bibliotek" (a library) and "et kort" (a card). To say a map, use the same word "kort": "Jeg har et kort over byen" (I have a map of the city).

et bidrag.explanation: "Et bidrag" means "a contribution". The word is also in "børnebidrag" (child support), a regular payment.

et billede.explanation: "Et billede" means "a picture". To say you take a picture, use "at tage et billede": "Må jeg tage et billede?" (May I take a picture?). For a picture taken with a camera, you can also use "et foto" (a photo): "Jeg tog et foto af huset" (I took a photo of the house).

et bind.explanation: "Et bind" means "a volume", as in one book of a set. It comes from the verb "at binde" (to tie). To say which one, put the number after it: "bind 2" (volume 2).

et bindeord.explanation: "Et bindeord" means "a conjunction". It is built from "at binde" (to tie) and "et ord" (a word). To join two parts of a sentence, use one such as "og" (and): "Jeg spiser og drikker" (I eat and drink).

et biord.explanation: "Et biord" means "an adverb". It is built from "bi-" (side) and "et ord" (a word), so literally it is a "side word". To say how something is done, use one such as "hurtigt" (quickly): "Han løber hurtigt" (He runs quickly).

et bistade.explanation: "Et bistade" means "a beehive". Another word for it is "en bikube" (a beehive): "Han passer sin bikube" (He looks after his beehive).

et bjerg.explanation: "Et bjerg" means "a mountain". A famous Danish one, "Himmelbjerget" (the Sky Mountain), is only about 150 metres high. For a lower rise, use "en bakke" (a hill): "Vi cykler op ad en bakke" (We cycle up a hill).

et blad.explanation: "Et blad" means "a magazine / a leaf". To talk about the leaf of a tree, say: "Træet har grønne blade" (The tree has green leaves). The word is also in "et dagblad" (a daily newspaper).

et blik.explanation: "Et blik" means "a look". To say someone glanced at something, use "at kaste et blik på" (to cast a glance at): "Han kastede et blik på uret" (He glanced at the clock).

et blinklys.explanation: "Et blinklys" means "a turn signal". It is built from "blink" (blink) and "et lys" (a light). To say you signal, use "at blinke" (to blink): "Jeg blinker til højre" (I signal right).

et blomsterbed.explanation: "Et blomsterbed" means "a flower bed". It is built from "en blomst" (a flower) and "et bed" (a bed). To talk about a bed of vegetables, use "et bed" alone: "et bed med gulerødder" (a bed of carrots).

et blåbær.explanation: "Et blåbær" means "a blueberry". It is built from "blå" (blue) and "et bær" (a berry); "blå" is also in "en blåhval" (a blue whale).

et blåt mærke.explanation: "Et blåt mærke" means "a bruise". Literally, it is "a blue mark". After "et" the word is "blåt", but after "det" it is "blå": "det blå mærke" (the bruise).

et boardingpas.explanation: "Et boardingpas" means "a boarding pass". For the book you carry to travel abroad, use "et pas" (a passport): "Jeg viser mit pas" (I show my passport).

et bogstav.explanation: "Et bogstav" means "a letter (of the alphabet)". For a letter you send in the post, use "et brev" (a letter): "Jeg skriver et brev" (I am writing a letter).

et boligmarked.explanation: "Et boligmarked" means "a housing market". It is built from "en bolig" (a home) and "et marked" (a market). To say you want to buy a home, use "at købe bolig" (to buy a home): "Vi vil købe bolig" (We want to buy a home).

et bonuskort.explanation: "Et bonuskort" means "a loyalty card". It is built from "bonus" (a reward) and "et kort" (a card).

et bord.explanation: "Et bord" means "a table". To ask for a table in a restaurant, say: "Et bord til to, tak" (A table for two, please). For a desk, use "et skrivebord" (literally, a writing table): "Jeg sidder ved mit skrivebord" (I am sitting at my desk).

et brag.explanation: "Et brag" means "a bang / crash". To say something ended with a big finish, use "med et brag" (with a bang): "Festen sluttede med et brag" (The party ended with a bang).

et brandvæsen.explanation: "Et brandvæsen" means "a fire department". It is built from "en brand" (a fire) and "et væsen" (a service); "væsen" is also in "sundhedsvæsenet" (the health service). In Denmark, you call 112 for the fire department.

et brev.explanation: "Et brev" means "a letter". For an email, use "en mail" (an email): "Jeg sender en mail" (I am sending an email).

et brud.explanation: "Et brud" means "a break / breach". To say a rule or agreement is not kept, use "et brud på" (a breach of): "et brud på aftalen" (a breach of the agreement). To talk about the end of a relationship, use the same word: "et brud mellem dem" (a break-up between them). Do not mix it up with "en brud" (a bride), which is an en-word: "Bruden smiler" (The bride smiles).

et brugernavn.explanation: "Et brugernavn" means "a username". It is built from "en bruger" (a user) and "et navn" (a name); "navn" is also in "et fornavn" (a first name).

et brusebad.explanation: "Et brusebad" means "a shower", as in washing yourself. To say you take one, use "at tage" (to take): "Jeg tager et brusebad efter træning" (I take a shower after exercise).

et bruseforhæng.explanation: "Et bruseforhæng" means "a shower curtain". It is built from "bruse-" (shower) and "et forhæng" (a curtain).

et bryggeri.explanation: "Et bryggeri" means "a brewery". It is built from "at brygge" (to brew). Carlsberg is a well-known Danish brewery.

et bryggers.explanation: "Et bryggers" means "a utility room". To say where the washing hangs, use "i bryggerset" (in the utility room): "Tøjet hænger i bryggerset" (The clothes are hanging in the utility room).

et bryllup.explanation: "Et bryllup" means "a wedding". To say you are going to a wedding, use "til bryllup": "Vi skal til bryllup i morgen" (We are going to a wedding tomorrow).

et bryst.explanation: "Et bryst" means "a chest", as in the front of the upper body. Danish says "brystet" (the chest) where English says "my chest": "Jeg har smerter i brystet" (I have pain in my chest). The word also means "a breast". To talk about the meat, use "et kyllingebryst" (a chicken breast).

et bræt.explanation: "Et bræt" means "a board", as in a flat piece of wood. To talk about more than one, use the plural "brædder": "tre brædder" (three boards). The word is also in "et strygebræt" (an ironing board).

et brætspil.explanation: "Et brætspil" means "a board game". It is built from "et bræt" (a board) and "et spil" (a game); "bræt" is also in "et skærebræt" (a cutting board).

et bud.explanation: "Et bud" means "an offer / bid". To say what you think will happen, use it for a guess: "Mit bud er, at han kommer" (My guess is that he will come). To name a messenger, use it in "et cykelbud" (a bike courier).
